title: Morphling: A Throughput-Maximized TFHE-based Accelerator using Transform-domain Reuse
problem: TFHE bootstrapping requires over 10,000 polynomial multiplications at 128-bit security level, with domain-transform operations (FFT) consuming up to 88% of computational overhead and creating the primary bottleneck in TFHE systems.
motivation: Fully Homomorphic Encryption enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data in cloud computing, but its extreme computational requirements limit practical deployment.
method: Morphling combines a 2D systolic array architecture with strategic transform-domain reuse to reduce FFT redundancy by up to 83.3%. The design includes merge-split pipelined-FFT for efficient domain transformation, a double-pointer method for high-throughput polynomial rotation, and specialized buffer design optimized for TFHE operations with custom instructions for tiling and batching.
key_novelty: Strategic reuse of transform-domain computations (FFT results) across multiple TFHE operations to reduce redundant domain transformations by up to 83.3%.
contributions: Transform-domain reuse optimization reducing FFT overhead by up to 83.3%, enabling more computational cores in the same die area
Specialized microarchitecture including merge-split pipelined-FFT, double-pointer polynomial rotation, and custom instruction set for TFHE
Demonstrated performance of 147,615 bootstrappings/sec (3440x CPU, 143x GPU, 14.7x SOTA) with sub-second deep learning inference

metrics.speedup: 3440x over CPU, 143x over GPU, 14.7x over SOTA TFHE accelerator
metrics.other: 147,615 bootstrappings/sec, 53W power consumption, sub-second latency for deep learning models

primary_theme: FHE accelerator via transform-domain reuse and systolic dataflow
